title: Justice System Adventure
welcome_lead: Police, courts, prisons — meet the justice system. 👮
meta_desc: Crime & Society Adventure 3 — KS3 Sociology on the UK criminal justice system.
final_note: You met the UK justice system and what happens after a crime.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Steps after a crime:

  • Police investigate and may arrest.
  • The Crown Prosecution Service decides whether to charge.
  • The court hears the case.

Magistrates' courts handle small cases.

Crown Court handles serious cases with a jury of 12 ordinary citizens.

Sentences include:

  • Fines.
  • Community service.
  • Suspended sentence.
  • Prison.

Rehabilitation tries to help offenders change. Some prisons offer education and work programmes. 📚

mcqs.q: What do feminists mean by the 'dark side' of family life?
options: The reality that families can be sites of inequality, exploitation and violence — particularly affecting women and children — challenging functionalist portrayals of the family as universally beneficial.
The 'dark side' refers to families who live in poverty.
Schools have no influence on outcomes.
The 'dark side' is a metaphor about families who don't communicate.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between reliability and validity in research?
options: Reliability is whether a method produces consistent results when repeated; validity is whether it actually measures what it claims to. A method can be reliable but invalid, or valid but unreliable.
Reliable research is published in journals; valid research isn't.
Schools have no influence on outcomes.
Reliable and valid mean the same thing — that the research is good.
